reviewStatus: Drafted from primary sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
name: Spinal Instability Neoplastic Score

version.label: SOSG SINS (Fisher et al. 2010)
version.detail: Six components, total 0–18. Categories 0–6 stable, 7–12 potentially unstable, 13–18 unstable.

purpose: Assessment of tumour-related spinal instability to support referral and multidisciplinary discussion.
intendedPopulation: Adults with primary or metastatic neoplastic involvement of the spine (assessed per affected level).

inputDefinitions.label: Pain
inputDefinitions.help: Mechanical pain: relief with recumbency and/or pain with movement or loading of the spine.

options.label: No collapse, more than 50% of body involved

inputDefinitions.label: Posterolateral involvement
inputDefinitions.help: Facet, pedicle or costovertebral joint fracture, or replacement with tumour.

resultStates.label: Potentially unstable
resultStates.detail: In the original SINS publication, scores of 7–18 were considered to warrant surgical consultation. Integrate with neurological status, histology, prognosis and patient goals.

resultStates.label: Unstable
resultStates.detail: In the original SINS publication, scores of 7–18 were considered to warrant surgical consultation. Integrate with neurological status, histology, prognosis and patient goals.

clinicalInsights.text: SINS assesses mechanical stability only; neurological compression, histology and prognosis are assessed separately.
Intermediate scores have the most inter-observer variation; component-level review helps multidisciplinary discussion.
Mechanical pain is a major contributor and reflects clinical, not only radiological, assessment.

limitations: Designed for neoplastic disease, not trauma or infection.
Agreement is lower in the potentially unstable range.
Assessed per level; multi-level disease needs level-by-level scoring.
confounders: Osteoporotic fracture at the same level
Pain from causes other than the lesion
commonErrors: Using the wrong junctional boundaries (e.g. C7–T2, T11–L1).
Scoring alignment from supine imaging alone without noting it.

guideSections.what: A six-component score (location, pain, bone lesion, alignment, collapse, posterolateral involvement) for tumour-related spinal instability; totals range 0–18.
guideSections.whenUseful: Communicating instability between oncology, radiation oncology, radiology and spine surgery; screening for referral.
guideSections.howToCalculate: Score the affected level on each component using clinical history and CT/MRI, then sum.
guideSections.clinicalContext: One input to multidisciplinary decisions, alongside neurology, oncology, mechanical instability and systemic disease frameworks.

sources.citation: Fisher CG, DiPaola CP, Ryken TC, et al. A novel classification system for spinal instability in neoplastic disease: an evidence-based approach and expert consensus from the Spine Oncology Study Group. Spine. 2010;35(22):E1221-E1229.
Fourney DR, Frangou EM, Ryken TC, et al. Spinal instability neoplastic score: an analysis of reliability and validity from the Spine Oncology Study Group. J Clin Oncol. 2011;29(22):3072-3077.
